newsitem.title: INDONESIA: One shot dead in Jakarta campaign violence - report.
newsitem.headline: One shot dead in Jakarta campaign violence - report.

text.p: A bystander was shot dead during clashes in the Indonesian capital Jakarta between security forces and supporters of a Moslem-oriented minority party, the Republika newspaper reported on Wednesday.

The paper said 20-year-old Adam Khaeruddin was shot while watching the disturbances in the Warung Buncit area of south Jakarta on Tuesday afternoon as a number of districts in the south and east of the city were hit by violence in the run-up to voting on May 29.

The report did not say who fired the fatal shot, although witnesses said both police and troops fired warning shots in the air to disperse the crowd of a few thousand supporters of the Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP).
Neither hospitals nor police were immediately available for comment on the report.

Lieutenant-General Syarwan Hamid, head of the military's socio-political section, was quoted by the Kompas daily on Wednesday as saying 110 people had died in accidents, 100 were seriously injured and 400 slightly hurt since the campaign began on April 27.

Hamid said 83 people had died in traffic accidents and 27 drowned when a boat they were on sank on the way to a Golkar rally. However news reports have said one Golkar member was killed in an attack by unknown assailants in the city of Yogyakarta earlier this month.

Political analysts have said the ruling Golkar party is expected to win easily the elections for 425 seats in parliament. The rest of the seats in the 500-member house are reserved for the military, which does not vote.
